title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: c_{a,b} = (a+b)!/(a! b!) are binomial coefficients, i.e. the structure constants of a divided-power algebra (x^{[a]} x^{[b]} = c_{a,b} x^{[a+b]}). A fixed index i is given, together with a family (ξ_k)_{k≥N} of elements of a Z_p-module M satisfying the compatibilities (1). In the form used on the next page these read c_{l,j+i} ξ_h = c_{l,j} ξ_{h'} for h = i+j and h' = h+l. Such relations arise when one checks a uniqueness or vanishing statement for a compatible system in the divided-power (PD) de Rham setting, for instance a PD Poincaré-lemma type computation.

The previous page reduces the problem to a Corollary: if ξ_{h0} = 0 for some h0 with c_{i,h0-i} a p-adic unit, then ξ_k = 0 for all k. This page begins the proof in two steps.

Lemma 1: ξ_k = 0 for every k ≥ N with c_{i,k-i} ≢ 0 mod p.

Lemma 1.1 (connecting step): let k' ≥ k ≥ N, j = k-i, j' = k'-i, with c_{i,j} and c_{i,j'} both units.
- Then c_{j'-j,j} is a unit if and only if c_{j'-j,j+i} is a unit.
- When these hold, relation (1) with l = j'-j shows ξ_k = 0 if and only if ξ_{k'} = 0.

Proof of 1.1: compute in Q. Both ratios c_{j'-j,j+i}/c_{j'-j,j} and c_{i,j'}/c_{i,j} equal (i+j')! j! / ((i+j)! j'!). This is the trinomial identity c_{l,i+j} c_{i,j} = c_{i,j+l} c_{l,j} = (i+j+l)!/(i! j! l!). The second ratio is a quotient of two units of Z_p, so the two coefficients in (5) have the same p-adic valuation.

The next page completes Lemma 1 using base-p digits (Lucas/Kummer). Any admissible k is linked to the common index k' = i+j' = p^{r+1}-1, whose digits are j'_α = p-1-i_α. All admissible indices are therefore 'connected', and vanishing propagates from h0 to all of them.
errors: No mathematical error. The (a)=(b) identity is correct: both equal (i+j')! j! / ((i+j)! j'!).
A crossed-out attempt to argue via '(i+j)! ~ i! j!' up to units was abandoned in favour of the cleaner exact identity in Q.
Lemma 1 is stated loosely: its hypothesis ξ_{h0} = 0 with c_{i,h0-i} a unit is inherited implicitly from the Corollary on the previous page.

ideas.what: Equality of binomial ratios c_{l,i+j}/c_{l,j} = c_{i,j+l}/c_{i,j} (associativity of divided-power multiplication / trinomial coefficient)
ideas.modern_name: Trinomial / multinomial identity; associativity of the divided-power algebra Γ

ideas.what: Propagation of vanishing in a compatible system indexed by k, using p-adic unit binomial coefficients and connectivity through indices p^r - 1
ideas.modern_name: Lucas' theorem / Kummer carries argument in PD-algebra computations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lucas (1878), Kummer; standard in crystalline cohomology (Berthelot)

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary, correct p-adic binomial-coefficient lemma serving a routine uniqueness step in a divided-power computation; nothing new beyond standard Lucas/Kummer arguments.
transcription_corrections: In (5) the right-hand coefficient is c_{j'-j, j+i} (the 'j+j'-looking scribble is corrected to j+i), consistent with the computation in (a).
In Lemma 1 the insertion above the line reads 'k≥N tel que' and modifies the condition c_{i,k-i} ≢ 0 (p).
In the final paragraph the reading 'deux unités de Z_p' (with 'p-adiques' struck out) and 'l'un est une unité ssi l'autre l'est' is consistent with the image.
